rules: Unknown abundance is null, not zero.
Gene entries, protein groups, proteoforms, complexes and chemical species have different counting units.
A group estimate is never assigned separately to each member.
HeLaM estimates are not transferred to the diploid G1 model.
Ion elemental totals include bound pools; do not double count bound states.
Family rows are an expansion checklist, not individually resolved molecular species.
Structure provenance, abundance provenance, and placement provenance must remain separate.
Predicted/integrative structures and flexible missing regions are not fully measured atomic coordinates.

source_inventory.record_preservation: Original protein/molecule source_record fields are unchanged; normalized identifiers are separate.

uniprot_cross_reference_snapshot.scope: Reviewed human UniProtKB entries; references only, not coordinate files or reviewed model selections
uniprot_cross_reference_snapshot.interpretation: A recorded reference is not a downloaded, selected, complete or scientifically reviewed structure.

rules: Identity registration and a structure cross-reference do not mean a coordinate asset exists locally.
Current coordinate availability is joined from the separate asset manifests, never inferred from this identity record.
A gene entry can encode several isoforms/proteoforms; never equate it automatically with one full-length structure.
PDB cross-references may describe fragments, mutants, complexes or different states; they require selection and review.
AlphaFold references are predicted models; resolve actual metadata/download URLs and confidence before use.
Missing reviewed-UniProt mapping is not evidence of protein or structure absence.
Unknown counts are null; the separate HeLa reference does not populate the default G1 model.
RNA and lipid family records require concrete sequence/species identities before coordinate selection.
No atoms, missing residues, protonation states, chromosome folds, or population counts are generated here.

structural_candidates.name: Canonical human H3.1 nucleosome core particle

organism.nucleic_acid_source: 146-bp experimental DNA construct; not a mapped genomic locus

assembly.description: Histone octamer: two copies each of H3.1, H4, H2A and H2B, with a 146-bp DNA duplex.

coverage.scope_note: RCSB entry-level counts, not physiological abundance or a guarantee of canonical-sequence completeness.

suggested_representations: deposited atoms in a local view
limitations: The associated paper compares H3T and H3.1; this specific entry is the canonical H3.1 structure, not the testis-specific H3T entry.
Unresolved histone regions and hydrogen atoms must remain absent unless a separate explicitly modeled representation is added.
A crystal nucleosome does not specify chromosome folding, nucleosome spacing, epigenetic state, or local abundance.
Retain existing 2CV5 as the working template; replacing it is lower priority than adding other molecular categories.

structural_candidates.name: Human PCNA sliding-clamp trimer

coverage.scope_note: RCSB entry-level counts; no nuclear copy number is inferred.

limitations: This entry contains the clamp, without DNA, polymerase or a complete repair/replication assembly.
A G1 environment must not use its placement to imply active S-phase replication forks.
Trimer abundance and PCNA polypeptide abundance are different quantities; the assembly contains three PCNA chains.
Preserve gaps and unresolved terminal residues.

structural_candidates.name: Human nucleophosmin 1 pentameric core

assembly.structural_scope: Ordered core from a partially disordered full-length protein preparation

coverage.scope_note: Only the resolved core is represented. These counts describe the deposited construct, not a complete pentameric molecular envelope.

suggested_representations: separately labeled flexible-region extent if later modeled
limitations: The majority of the deposited sequence lacks resolved coordinates; do not present the compact core as the whole physical extent of full-length NPM1.
Disordered acidic regions and flexible C-terminal interactions do not have one fixed experimentally resolved conformation in this entry.
NPM1 pentamers and their five constituent chains must not be counted as six independent molecular populations.
4N8M is a mouse NPM1 domain structure; use this verified human entry for the human environment.

structural_candidates.name: Human Ku70–Ku80 heterodimer bound to DNA

assembly.description: Ku70–Ku80 heterodimer with a DNA-end substrate.

coverage.scope_note: Entry/construct coverage is not full-length physiological-complex completeness.

limitations: The Ku80 construct is shorter than the full protein and some deposited regions remain unresolved.
The structure does not include DNA-PKcs, ligase IV or the complete nonhomologous end-joining machinery.
Use a specifically identified illustrative DNA-repair site; do not imply that every chromatin region is broken.
Ku70, Ku80, the Ku assembly and its DNA substrate require explicit membership accounting, not additive abundance rows.

structural_candidates.name: Human PARP1 activation domains bound to a DNA break

assembly.description: Zn1, Zn3 and WGR–CAT domain constructs assembled on a DNA break; assembly 2 is another deposited assembly choice.
assembly.structural_scope: Domain-based reconstruction of a monomeric PARP1 activation arrangement

coverage.scope_note: Entry contains multiple construct copies. Pin one biological assembly and do not equate three construct chains with three physiological PARP1 molecules.

suggested_representations: domain cartoons with source chain labels
limitations: This is not a complete full-length PARP1 structure.
Three separate experimental domain chains represent parts of one physiological protein; the PDB heteromer label is not a nuclear population count.
Missing domains/linkers must not be silently connected by invented atomic coordinates.
The DNA-bound activation conformation is a particular biochemical state.

structural_candidates.name: Human RNA polymerase II elongation complex

assembly.description: Twelve-subunit human Pol II with DNA and RNA in an intermediate translocation state.

coverage.scope_note: RCSB entry-level counts. Missing flexible regions are not supplied by the reported global resolution.

suggested_representations: selected subunit or spatial atomic chunk
limitations: The source is one translocation state, not a trajectory or complete transcription factory.
Do not fill flexible/unresolved Pol II regions or the full CTD with a single apparently measured conformation.
The associated study also contains RECQL5-bound structures; 9EHZ itself is the Pol II elongation-complex reference listed here.
The deposited atom count exceeds BioSim's current 20,000-atom template cap, so a generic importer and chunked atomic endpoint are needed.
Prefer this verified human complex over pig/human mixed Pol II assemblies unless mixed species are explicitly intended.

structural_candidates.name: Human 17S U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein

assembly.description: Twenty protein-chain components with U2 snRNA; a preassembly/branch-site proofreading-related 17S U2 state.

coverage.scope_note: Substantial sequence is unresolved even at a 2.50 Å reported global resolution.

limitations: This is U2 snRNP, not U1 or a whole spliceosome.
The assembly is state-specific; it should not be substituted for every snRNP in the nucleus.
A large fraction of the deposited sequence is unresolved or flexible; preserve that coverage information.
Some constituents also occur in assembled spliceosomes, so population bookkeeping must distinguish free/available snRNPs from bound assembly members.

structural_candidates.name: Human post-catalytic spliceosome, P complex

organism.nucleic_acid_source: Deposited spliceosomal RNAs and experimental pre-mRNA/exon substrate

assembly.description: Human post-catalytic P-complex assembly with ligated exon retained.

coverage.scope_note: The reported global resolution does not establish every peripheral region or every deposited residue.

suggested_representations: selected active-site or subunit atomic chunk
limitations: Spliceosome composition changes during assembly, catalysis and disassembly; this is not a universal static spliceosome.
Do not populate the scene with full complexes plus separately counted copies of all of their bound constituents.
Unresolved peripheral regions remain absent.
A whole-complex ball-and-stick mesh would exceed the current nucleosome-focused memory strategy; use subassembly and spatial LOD.

structural_candidates.name: Human RNA polymerase I elongation complex, post-translocation state

assembly.description: Thirteen-subunit human Pol I with DNA and RNA.

coverage.scope_note: RCSB entry-level counts; flexible stalk and unresolved regions require explicit coverage metadata.

suggested_representations: assembly surface near a schematic nucleolar rDNA site
limitations: Pol I transcribes rRNA precursor genes; this is not Pol II and should not be scattered as a generic transcription enzyme.
This is a specific experimental translocation state.
The structure does not supply the surrounding rDNA chromatin, nucleolar layout or molecule count.
Global resolution should not be applied uniformly to flexible peripheral regions.

structural_candidates.name: Human small-subunit processome, nucleolar post-A1 state

assembly.description: Human SSU processome after A1 processing; a large RNA/protein ribosome-biogenesis assembly.

coverage.scope_note: RCSB entry-level counts include an experimentally assigned subset of a large, flexible assembly; one deposited entity is explicitly unassigned peptides.

limitations: This is a nucleolar ribosome precursor assembly, not a mature translating cytoplasmic ribosome.
The post-A1 conformation is one state in a maturation pathway.
Keep unidentified peptide regions unidentified; do not assign invented protein identities.
Requires chunking and strict geometry budgets; do not construct hundreds of thousands of Python atom spheres for every displayed processome.
Processome constituents overlap with ribosomal-protein and RNA populations; avoid double counting.

structural_candidates.name: Human lamin A/C N-terminal fragment tetramer

assembly.description: Tetrameric arrangement of two antiparallel coiled-coil dimers from an approximately 1–300 lamin fragment.
assembly.structural_scope: Experimental lamin fragment and assembly-interface reference

coverage.scope_note: Construct coverage does not represent full-length lamin A/C. The deposited chains include selenomethionine.

limitations: This is not a complete atomic human lamin filament or a measured nuclear lamina network.
Missing C-terminal portions and unobserved linkers cannot be stitched into an apparently experimental full-length structure.
Repeating fragments into a long lamina polymer is a separate modeling step with separate provenance.
Selenomethionine is an experimental chemical derivative; preserve and label it rather than silently dropping HETATM polymer residues or converting Se to S.
Lamin A and lamin C share sequence but differ at the C terminus; this shared fragment does not distinguish complete isoforms.

structural_candidates.name: Dilated human nuclear pore complex, integrative structural model

organism.expression_system: In-cell structural context plus component models

structural_candidates.method: Integrative modeling combining cryo-electron tomography/subtomogram averaging, component structures and AI-based prediction
structural_candidates.resolution_scope: Resolution of the associated in-cell cryo-ET map, not atom-level accuracy of every fitted component

assembly.description: C8-symmetric dilated NPC assembly; archive lists an 808-protein-chain assembly model.
assembly.structural_scope: Large integrative scaffold model, not a completely experimentally resolved atomic pore

coverage.scope_note: RCSB entry-level summary; inspect assembly operators before expanding geometry. Generated biological-assembly counts can differ. None of these numbers is a whole-nucleus pore count.

suggested_representations: reusable scaffold-sector/subunit meshes with assembly transforms
source-specific atomic subunits only when their individual provenance supports them
limitations: Do not label all fitted atomic coordinates as directly measured: AI predictions and integrative fitting are integral to this model.
Intrinsically disordered FG regions and linker populations cannot be shown as one fully resolved rigid channel barrier.
This is a dilated state; pore geometry responds to biological context and membrane tension.
Import assembly transforms explicitly and reuse sectors/subunits; the whole pore is far beyond the current single-nucleosome atom budget.
The displayed pore-marker count in BioSim remains a sampling choice, independent of the subunit stoichiometry of one NPC.
The related 7TBJ title refers to a 12 Å map while its RCSB resolution field currently reports 23 Å; avoid copying a resolution solely from an entry title.

structural_review.scope: Source-verified structural import candidates for BioSim's illustrative human interphase nuclear environment. This is a structural asset shortlist, not a complete nuclear molecular inventory or an abundance ranking.
structural_review.verification: RCSB entry pages and linked primary-paper metadata were inspected. EMD-14321 map resolution was independently checked in EMDB. No coordinate imports, application code, tests or benchmarks were executed for this research.

count_conventions.abundance: Not estimated here. Protein chains, molecules, complexes and display instances require separate population accounting.
count_conventions.entry_statistics: Reported atom/residue counts are RCSB entry-level summaries. They may include multiple crystallographic copies or differ from the expanded biological assembly. They must not be used as nuclear molecule counts.
count_conventions.completeness: Modeled/deposited residue counts refer to the experimental construct. A high modeled fraction does not establish full canonical-protein coverage.
count_conventions.resolution: Reported global experimental resolution is not uniform local coordinate accuracy. Integrative or predicted components retain separate provenance.
count_conventions.placement: Placing any of these structures into BioSim remains illustrative unless a compatible spatial dataset is separately supplied.

implementation_notes: Current Frame.sphere in sim/nucleus_view.py draws pygame discs. True molecular shape requires coordinate-derived or map-derived 3D meshes, not just replacing marker labels.

Current sim/nucleosome_asset.py and tools/import_nucleosome.py are deliberately 2CV5-specific, with a 20,000-atom cap and DNA/protein residue whitelist. Do not apply their fixed identity checks to unrelated structures.

A generic import manifest must identify PDB version/hash, assembly/operator selection, organism per entity, source units, residue and atom coverage, modified residues, alternate-location policy, retained cofactors, provenance and derived representation hashes.

The present policy excluding all HETATM cannot be transferred blindly: other candidates contain structural metals or modified polymer residues. Curate retention per entity/chemical component; crystallization solvent remains distinct from physiological nucleoplasm.

Existing sim/pdb_import.py infers display bonds, while the nucleosome path intentionally infers none. A generic scientific import should use trusted connectivity/chemical-component definitions and preserve chain breaks rather than silently invoking distance-based inference.

Reuse sim/multiscale.py SceneNode.geometry_key, float64 nanometre placements, rigid angstrom conversion, culling and hysteresis; reuse sim/detail_cache.py shared worker, global in-flight gate and bounded assets.

GPUProteinRenderer currently has one geometry_key/VAO. Calling its single-object draw repeatedly for different asset types will replace GPU buffers and repeatedly read back the framebuffer. Add a nucleus-only batched pass with per-asset GPU meshes and one shared depth buffer/readback while preserving ordinary molecule rendering.

Keep population/species/assembly membership separate from structural representation. A nucleosome, its eight histones and its DNA are one nested assembly accounting choice, not ten additive independent population entries.

Start with existing 2CV5 plus small verified PCNA, NPM1-core and Ku/DNA assets. Add larger polymerase/snRNP assemblies as surfaces/backbones with selected atomic chunks; introduce spliceosome/processome/NPC full-assembly surfaces only after chunking.

A nuclear overview may use schematic 3D membrane meshes and irregular chromatin/nucleolar density volumes. Label generated density as educational; it is not an electron-microscopy map of a measured nucleus.

checked_but_not_primary_choices.reason: Human U1 snRNP at 5.49 Å with 3365 reported atoms for 3361 modeled residues; suitable for a trace-level architectural representation, not an invented full-atom endpoint.
Human-protein minimal U1 snRNP at 3.30 Å; heavily engineered RNA and truncated protein constructs. Use only under an explicit engineered-minimal-U1 label.
Human pre-A complex at 3.00 Å includes an adenovirus-derived RNA substrate; organism metadata must remain per entity.
Pol II–DSIF–SPT6–U1 complex contains pig and human components plus synthetic construct. Do not silently substitute it as wholly human.
Lamin–nucleosome interaction entry contains Xenopus laevis and human components. Useful cross-species interaction evidence, not an all-human native-lamina filament.
